concepts: Quick actions

Short guided requests such as Request Leave, Get Payslip or Monthly Attendance. Each one asks its questions one at a time in a small popup (a date, a dropdown, a remark…) and submits the request at the end. When it finishes you can Continue with another request or Cancel to close.
HR Mate
The product help assistant. Ask how to do something in 247HRM — it answers with step-by-step instructions. It explains the screens; it does not change your data.
Company Policy
The policy assistant. Ask about the rules your company has published — leave entitlement, attendance, travel, conduct and so on. Answers are based on your company policies.

concepts: Post

A timeline entry you create. It can carry plain text, uploaded images, a video (YouTube or direct MP4 link), an appreciation badge, or a poll. Posts can be sent to specific employees and are limited to 250 words.
Appreciation (badge)
A special post that recognises one or more colleagues. You pick the employee(s) and a badge; the recognition then appears under the recipient's Achievements and shows who earned the badge.
Poll

A question with multiple options that you send to selected employees. You set the options (2 or more) and a duration (1 Day, 3 Days, 1 Week, 15 Days or 30 Days). People vote while the poll is open; results (percentages and vote counts) show once they have voted, the poll closes, or for the poll creator.
Vote / Undo
While a poll is open you can pick one option to vote. If you change your mind you can Undo your vote before the poll closes. After the duration ends the poll is closed and shows only the result.
Reactions

Six emoji responses - Like, Love, Haha, Wow, Sad, Angry - you can add to a post or comment. Hovering the Like button opens the picker; each person has one reaction at a time, which you can change or Clear. Click the count to see who reacted.
Pinned post

A post you mark with the pin so it stays at the top of the timeline and appears in the Pinned Posts widget. Pinning shows "added to the pinned section" and unpinning shows "removed from the pinned section". Use the timeline filter to view only Pinned posts.
Block / Hide vs Report

Block/Hide simply hides a post from your own view (you can unblock it later from Activities). Report is moderation: you pick a category (Nudity, Violence, Harassment, Hate or Other), review the matching community-standard details, and Submit - this flags the post for review.
RewardKart points

A points wallet. Eligible users (managers/admins) can share points from their own balance to an employee - you must pick at least one employee and an amount that is above zero and within your balance. Your earned reward points can be redeemed via the Claim/Reward link.
Tasks
A simple to-do board opened from the timeline, with Begin, In Progress and End columns. You can add a task and set its status (a 250-word AI-assisted note) to track work alongside the social feed.
Activities

A running log in the sidebar. "My Activities" shows what you did (posted, appreciated, commented, replied, reacted, deleted); "Others Activities" shows what others did on your posts and comments. Blocked/hidden posts can be unblocked from here.
Sidebar widgets

Quick previews on the right: Birthdays, Work Anniversary and Newly Joined (people lists with dates), Achievements (badges you earned), Images and Videos (your uploads, deletable on hover), Polls and Pinned Posts. "See All" opens the full list.

path: Implementation checklist
summary: Configure in this order: each step feeds dropdowns and calculations in the next. Skipping ahead is the most common cause of missing dropdown values and wrong first payrolls.

2. Organization masters: Location → Department → Section → Designation → Grade → Employment Type → Cost Center → Bank Master → Finance Company → Custom Fields

4. Attendance: Pay Period → Shift Definition → Shift Patterns → Late Early → Over Time Rules → Incident → Leave Type → Dynamic WeekOff; then Holiday Management per state/location
5. Salary: Allowances → Deductions → Loans → Advances → Notice Period; Local Claim and Company Welfare masters if used
6. Workflow: Approval Configuration, Manage Ticketing Details, Notification settings
7. Employee data: Employee Management > Employees or Uploads (Existing Employees, Leave Opening Balance, Bank/Loans, TDS)

concepts: Swipe Embedded Settings

Controls whether holidays and weekly offs are "embedded" (counted as eligible) for swipe/biometric attendance. You choose the period to consider (before, after, or before-or-after the attendance period) and the conditions under which they count (employee physically present, paid leave applied, or coinciding with a weekly off/holiday). Weekly-off eligibility can instead be driven by a minimum number of present days.
Auto-approval (Leave / Incident)
When enabled, leave or incident requests are approved automatically after the number of days you specify. The day count field only appears - and is mandatory - when the toggle is on.
Prospective Employee mandatory fields
Flags that force Aadhaar, PAN, cancelled cheque, and bank/payment details to be supplied (with document upload) before a prospective employee record can proceed.
Password Reset Policy

Defines the password rules for the company: minimum and maximum length, whether special characters are required, forcing a password change on first login, and whether passwords expire after a set number of days.
Employee Search Scope
When the employee search bar is enabled, this sets how widely a user can search - Global, Company, Location, Department, Section, Grade, Employment Type, Cost Center, or Manager.

title: Roles
path: ⚙ Settings (top bar) > Roles
summary: Create roles and the permissions they grant, then assign those roles to employees, transfer access between employees, and set which menus are shown by default.
next: Open the Roles tab to create or edit a role and its permissions, then use Assign Roles to give it to employees.

Define a role and tick the permissions (tasks) it should grant
Map roles and an access scope to employees

concepts: Role vs Permission

A permission (task) is a single capability such as Create, Modify, View or Download on a specific feature. A role is a named bundle of those permissions. Employees are given roles, not individual permissions.
Permission tree (tasks)

Permissions are organised as a tree: feature groups (e.g. Attendance Management, Employee Master, Reports) contain features, each with action leaves like Create, Modify, Cancel, Delete, View, Download or Upload. The codes in brackets (e.g. 2.1.1) are the permission codes saved against the role.
Auto-selected View

When you tick any action on a feature, its View permission is automatically ticked and disabled, because you must be able to view a feature to act on it. Unticking all other actions releases View again.
MFA Always Required / Allow Trusted Device
Per-role security flags. MFA Always Required forces multi-factor authentication for users with this role; Allow Trusted Device lets them mark a device as trusted to reduce repeat MFA prompts.
Hierarchy vs Scope

Hierarchy access derives who the user can see from the reporting structure (their subordinates, optionally limited by a depth of 1-10 levels). Scope access instead grants access to an explicit set of Companies, Locations, Employment types, Grades, Departments and Designations.
Assignment vs Role
A role defines WHAT a user can do (permissions). An assignment here ties a role to an employee and defines OVER WHOM (which employees) those permissions apply.
Copy roles
The Copy flow replicates the role assignments of a source ("From") employee onto a destination ("To") employee, so the destination receives the same role set without rebuilding it.
Transfer vs Copy

Transfer moves authority from the source employee to the destination (the source is left without it). Copy (on the Assign Roles tab) duplicates the source's assignments to the destination while the source keeps them.
Authority
An employee's "authority" is the bundle of role assignments and access scope granted to them. Role Transfer reassigns that whole authority from the From employee to the To employee.
Default permissions vs role permissions

Role permissions (Roles List tab) define what a specific role can do. Default permissions here decide which menus are shown out-of-the-box to the standard Employee and Manager profiles, independent of custom roles.
Employee vs Manager permission
Two independent visibility toggles per menu: one controls whether the menu appears for self-service Employees, the other for Managers.
rules: You only see the tabs and actions you have permission for
The built-in Admin and DEFAULT_ROLE roles are protected and cannot be edited or deleted
A role must have at least one permission selected before it can be saved
tips: Set up roles first, then assign them to employees on the Assign Roles tab
Use Copy or Transfer to reuse an existing employee's access instead of rebuilding it

Trying to edit or delete Admin / DEFAULT_ROLE

Maps one or more roles plus an access scope (or a reporting hierarchy) to an employee, so the employee gets that role's permissions over the chosen set of employees. Moves an employee's role assignments (their authority) from one employee to another — the source employee's access is transferred to the destination employee. You can: Select a From Employee (an employee who currently holds role authority); Select a To Employee (an employee who does not yet hold authority); Click Transfer to move the roles, then see the result in the grid.

title: IP Security
path: ⚙ Settings (top bar) > IP Security
summary: Controls which networks/IP addresses can access the application: set the default Allow or Deny policy, enable IP restriction per feature, and maintain the list of allowed/denied IP rules.
next: Decide your default policy with the Allow/Deny toggle, then add IP rules for the addresses you want to explicitly allow or deny.
can: Set the default IP restriction type with the Allow / Deny toggle on the Restriction Configuration card
Enable or disable IP restriction per feature (e.g. Attendance, Global) using each feature's toggle
Switch to the IP restriction list tab to see all configured rules in a searchable, paginated grid
Add a new IP rule (name, restriction type, address type Range or Specific, the IP/range, description and status)
Edit or delete an existing IP rule
View the locations/IP list associated with a rule
concepts: Default restriction type (Allow vs Deny)

The baseline policy for IP access. Allow = a whitelist: only IPs you explicitly add as Allow can reach the app. Deny = a blacklist: the IPs you add as Deny are blocked and everyone else is allowed. Individual rules in the list refine this baseline.
IP restriction per feature

IP restriction can be switched on or off per feature (e.g. Attendance, Global). The toggle on each feature card enables/disables enforcement for that feature only, and the change is saved as soon as you flip it.
Address type: Range vs Specific

A rule can target a Specific single IP address, or a Range defined by a start and end IP (covering every address in between, e.g. a whole office subnet). The dialog shows the relevant IP fields based on which type you pick.
Active vs InActive rule
Each rule has a status. Only Active rules are enforced; setting a rule InActive keeps it in the list for later without applying it, which is safer than deleting and re-creating it.
Allow/Deny rule type

Independent of the address, each rule is tagged Allow (permit this IP/range) or Deny (block it). Together with the default policy, these decide whether a given source IP can use the restricted feature.
rules: The default restriction type (Allow / Deny) sets the baseline policy; individual IP rules then carry the exceptions in the rules list.
Allow as default means only the IPs you configure with type Allow can access (everything else is restricted); Deny as default means the configured Deny IPs are blocked and the rest are allowed.
IP restriction is applied per feature via each feature's Enable/Disable toggle — turning a feature off means it is not IP-restricted; toggling it saves immediately and shows the server message.
Adding/editing a rule requires Name, Restriction Type, Address Type and Description; the IP fields depend on the Address Type (Specific IP, or Range start + Range end).
Server-side validation rejects bad input per field — e.g. invalid Specific IP, invalid Range End IP, or a missing status ("Please give the status").
Deleting a rule goes through a confirmation dialog before it is removed.
A rule's status is shown as Active or InActive in the grid; only the rules you intend should be Active.
tips: Set the default policy first, then add the minimum set of rules needed — fewer, clearer rules are easier to audit.

concepts: Category vs Sub Category

Categories are the top-level buckets a help-desk ticket can belong to (e.g. Payroll, HR, IT). Sub Categories are the finer classifications under a category. Employees pick these when raising a ticket, and the routing rules here decide who handles each combination.
Authority
The employee (or employees) who receive and resolve tickets matching a rule. Assigning the right authority per category/scope ensures a raised ticket lands with the person responsible for that area.
Scope (Company / Location / Grade / Department / Designation / Employment Type / Section)

The audience a routing rule applies to. The same category can be routed to different authorities for different groups by setting these scopes; selecting all options for a scope stores "-1" meaning "applies to all".
Priority & TAT

Priority (e.g. High / Medium / Low) plus a TAT time and period (Minutes / Hours / Days) define the resolution target for tickets matched by the rule. This TAT is what the Help Desk screen later checks to flag whether a closed ticket met its SLA.
Forward To
The default forward route for the rule - where a ticket can be escalated/handed on if the primary authority cannot resolve it.

Encashable pays out unused leave within a min/max band; Carry Forward rolls a capped number of days into the next cycle; Negative Leaves lets the balance go below zero up to a defined limit.

Special leave accrues based on working a target weekday across selected week numbers each month, with its own validity window, monthly accrual count, a block weekday on which it cannot be submitted, and holiday handling.

concepts: Prospective Employee

A pre-onboarding candidate whose details are captured before they become a real employee. You record their profile, optionally let them complete their own form, and later transfer them into the employee master.
Status lifecycle

A prospect moves through Pending (created, not yet invited or submitted) - Mail Sent (a self-service form invite was emailed) - Submitted (the candidate completed and returned the form) - Transferred (converted into a real employee). Deleted records are removed from the active flow.
Send Mails / Reminder

Sends each selected prospect an email inviting them to fill in their own details through the self-service form. When a selected prospect has already been mailed (status Mail Sent), the button reads "Reminder" and re-sends the invite. A result list reports which emails succeeded or failed.
Transfer Employee

Converts a prospect into a real employee. You enter a New Emp Id and confirm; the system creates the employee under that ID and the prospect moves to the Transferred list. A result list shows the new Employee ID and any per-record errors.
Bulk Uploads

concepts: Authority Transfer

Reassigning a manager's or approver's approval authority — and the pending items waiting on them — to another person. It is used when someone leaves, resigns, or is on long leave, so requests like leave, attendance or claims keep flowing to a valid approver instead of getting stuck.
Old vs New Authority

The "old authority" is the employee currently holding the approval rights (the row in the list). The "new authority" is the person you pick in the "Select New Authority" column to take those rights over.

concepts: Pay Period
The pay cycle (configured under pay periods) that, together with the chosen month, defines which employees and date range payroll is run for. It must be selected before any summary data loads.
Summary cards (Gross / Payroll Processed / Yet to Payroll Process)

The three fixed cards at the top. Gross shows previous vs current total pay and employee counts; Payroll Processed shows what has been processed; Yet to Payroll Process shows the amount, employee count and pending approvals still to be handled — clicking it lists those employees.
Component cards

Re-orderable cards for each payroll component — Leaves, LOP, Attendance, Joinees, Resignees, Salary Changes, Allowances, Deductions, L & A, L & A Deductions, Overtime, Statutory, TDS, Budget and Stop Salaries — each showing previous vs current amounts and counts. Open a card for a charted drill-down with the underlying employees.
Trial Payroll
A preview run (opened from the Trial Payroll button) used to check attendance and payroll results before committing. It is a dry run — use it to validate figures before the Final run.
Final / Attendance & Payroll Process

The real multi-stage wizard that walks through Attendance Not Completed → Attendance Completed → Need to Calculate → Review → Locked (with a Deviation stage when applicable). From here you process attendance, calculate, lock, send for approval, and unlock or delete when corrections are needed.
LOP (Loss of Pay)

Unpaid days deducted from salary. LOP days are edited inline while processing attendance; the system caps LOP at the employee's total days and at total days minus leaves already applied, recomputing paid/present days from the change.
Yet to process employees
Employees whose payroll has not been processed for the selected month and pay period. The Yet to Payroll Process card opens a read-only list of them so you can see who still needs to be run.
Calculate vs Lock

Calculate generates the salary figures for selected employees (Calculate & Lock does both in one step). Lock freezes the calculated payroll so it is ready for payout/approval; a locked run must be unlocked and deleted before it can be re-run.
Payroll lock
Locking marks payroll as final and ready for payout. After locking, the only way to change it is to unlock and delete the run, then re-run — this protects already-finalised pay.
Approval (Send for Approval)

On clients with payroll approval enabled, calculated payroll can be sent for approval before payout. While the grid is filtered to "Approval Pending", the Lock and Send for Approval actions are blocked; under "Reopened / Rejected", rows rejected by an approver can be re-sent with Send for Approval once corrected.
Joinee handling

New joiners surface on the Joinees card (previous vs current joinee pay and counts). Use the card's Add/Upload actions to complete their master data and allowances so they are picked up in the run before you calculate.
Add / Upload card actions

The Add and Upload icons on a card are shortcuts that navigate to the matching screen — leave calendar/attendance, employee master, or the relevant uploads (Leaves, Joinee Allowance, Monthly Attendance, Loan/Advance, TDS) — to capture missing data, returning you to Payroll afterwards.
Payroll Settings
A dialog (gear icon) to choose which dashboard cards, Quick Info items and Quick Reports are shown. Selections are saved to the server; at most 10 reports can be selected at once.
Quick panel

The right-side panel (list icon) showing live counts — Active Users, Geo Tagged, Web Login — plus configured report shortcuts (Employee Master, PT Challan, ESI Monthly Upload, PF ECR, Bank Transfer, Accounting JV, pay registers, Swipe Report and any dynamic reports).
rules: A Pay Period must be selected before data loads — changing the month without one shows "Please select PayPeriod".
The summary cards only load once at least one employee is in the current selection.
Run order is sequential: complete Attendance → make any LOP adjustments → Calculate → Review → Lock (→ send for Approval where enabled).

In the Final wizard each stage carries the rule in its tooltip: attendance must be processed for all employees before payroll; review and correct LOP before calculating; review/delete/re-run calculated payroll before locking; once Locked it is ready for payout and must be unlocked and deleted before it can be re-run.

When editing LOP days, LOP cannot exceed the employee's total days ("LOP Days cannot be greater than employee total days") and cannot exceed total days minus leaves already applied ("The updated N LOP cannot be processed due to M leaves being applied"); an invalid value reverts.

On clients with payroll approval enabled, Lock and Send for Approval are blocked while the grid filter is "Approval Pending". Under "Reopened / Rejected", Lock stays blocked but Send for Approval works for rows whose Current Status is "Rejected By …" — a rejected payroll can be corrected and re-sent.
The LOP component card is permission-gated (permission code 13.17.2); without it the LOP action on the card is hidden.
Heavy actions (process / calculate / lock / swipe / approve) run in batches of 100 employees and return a per-employee result list titled "Payroll Process Result Information".
Payroll Settings allows at most 10 Quick Reports — once 10 are selected the remaining report options are disabled.

concepts: EMI

Advances are interest-free, so the schedule (View) shows just EMI Month, Amount and Status. Editing an installment redistributes the remaining amount evenly across the future months (the last month absorbs any rounding); the end-month row and Paid rows are locked.
Extend

Spread the same outstanding over more months to lower the EMI. Set the new No. of Pending Months (max 500); “Extended Months” is auto-derived and must be greater than 0 (max 100). Paid + new pending months cannot exceed the Advance Master’s Max Months. Remarks are required.
Top Up

Add more amount to a running advance and recompute it (principal only — no interest). Close
Fully settle and close the advance. The Closing Amount (the entire outstanding) is fixed — you only pick the Payment Type (Cheque needs a number) and add Remarks. The advance is then marked closed.
Download

concepts: Add Bonus Calculation (the rule)

Opens the form to define HOW bonus is computed: which Employment Types it covers, the minimum time employed and days worked to qualify, the gross-salary cap, the bonus percentage, the floor/ceiling on the bonus amount, the From/To months it covers and the month it is paid. Saving stores the rule (it does not yet pay anyone).
Calculate / Run bonus

Takes an existing rule plus the employees you selected and computes each employee's bonus for the rule period. It returns a result list with the projected bonus, the calculated bonus, the nominal amount and a remarks message per employee, so you can see who qualified.
Delete bonus
Removes the previously calculated bonus for the selected employees under a chosen rule and shows a per-employee result list (id, name, message). It does not delete the rule itself.
Percentage Bonus vs Projected Bonus Rate

Percentage Bonus is the statutory/agreed bonus rate used for the actual calculation. Projected Bonus Rate is an optional forecasting rate (defaults to 0) used to show a projected figure alongside the calculated bonus.
Gross Salary Limit & Bonus amount limits

Gross Salary Limit (max gross salary per month) caps the salary that is eligible for bonus. Min/Max Bonus Amount and Max Bonus Salary in Month then clamp the resulting monthly bonus to a floor and a ceiling, so a bonus never falls below the minimum or exceeds the maximum.
Minimum Wages (Include / Exclude)

Controls whether the statutory minimum wage is part of the salary base used for eligibility and the bonus calculation. "Exclude Minimum Wages" (the default) leaves it out; "Include Minimum Wages" counts it in.
Include Payslip & Adjust to Loan

Include Payslip adds the calculated bonus to the employee payslip and unlocks the Mode of Payment (Cash / Cheque / Bank). Adjust to Loan offsets the bonus against the employee's outstanding loan balance instead of paying it out in full.

concepts: Ex-gratia

A discretionary, goodwill payment the employer makes beyond the statutory bonus. It is not a legal obligation; here you define the rule (eligibility, salary limits, percentage and amount caps) and the system computes the amount per eligible employee.
Employment Type (Applies To)
The employment categories the rule applies to. You can pick more than one; the rule only computes ex-gratia for employees in the chosen types.
Min Time Employed (Months and Years)
The minimum service an employee must have completed to qualify, expressed as a months value and a years value (each 1 to 2 digits).
Min Days Worked
The minimum physically worked days in the From-to-To period for an employee to be eligible. Capped at 1000 days.
Minimum Gross Salary / Month
The gross-salary threshold used for eligibility against the rule.
Percentage Exgratia with Min / Max amount
Ex-gratia is computed as a percentage of the eligible base, then clamped between the Min Exgratia Amount and Max Exgratia Amount per month, and limited by the Max Exgratia Salary in Month.

title: Income Tax EMI
path: ☰ Menu > HR Admin > Finance > EMI
summary: Shows each employee's computed annual income tax for a financial year and how the remaining tax (TDS) is spread as monthly installments (EMI) from April to March, and lets you adjust and save those month-wise deductions.
next: Pick the Financial Year and employees, choose Projection or Actuals, then click Show TDS/EMI Data.

concepts: TDS EMI (monthly installment)

TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) on salary is collected monthly. This screen takes the employee's annual tax-to-pay and splits it into month-wise installments (EMI) from April to March, so payroll deducts the right amount each month.
Projection vs Actuals

Projection mode estimates the full-year tax and the planned monthly split based on declared income/exemptions. Actuals mode reflects what has actually been processed in payroll, so you can compare planned vs deducted.
Tax computation columns

Each row breaks the tax down: Total Gross Income, Exemptions and Standard Deduction give Taxable Income; Tax, Rebate, Cess, Surcharge and Marginal Relief give Total Tax; minus Tax Paid (incl. previous-employer/other-income TDS) gives Tax to Pay, which is what the months must add up to.
Editable vs locked months
Months whose payroll is already processed are locked (read-only). Only the remaining open months can be edited, and the balance tax is distributed across just those months.
Auto-redistribution

When you set one month's amount, the screen recalculates the leftover tax (Tax to Pay minus what is already fixed) and spreads it evenly across the other editable months, highlighting the recomputed cells so the year still totals correctly.
Tax regime (Old / New)

Each employee's tax is computed under their chosen regime (Old or New), shown in the Regime column. The regime determines which exemptions/slabs apply, which is why two employees with the same gross can have different tax.
Bulk Update result

Update EMI sends all loaded employees to the server in batches of 100 with a live progress bar, then shows a result dialog listing each employee with whether their EMI saved successfully and any message.

concepts: Settlement
Paying out an approved local claim to the employee (or company). Each settlement records the amount, the mode used and supporting details, and moves the claim from Approved to a Settled state.
Cash settlement
Pay the claim in cash. Capture the amount, a mode (To Company / To Employee), the date and remarks. Success shows "Cash Settlement Processed Successfully".
Cheque settlement
Pay by cheque. Capture the cheque number, date, in-favour-of name, amount and remarks. Success shows "cheque Settlement Processed Successfully".
Bank settlement

Pay by bank transfer. Capture beneficiary name, bank name, IFSC, branch, account number, amount and remarks (the employee's saved bank details pre-fill when available). Success shows "Bank Settlement Processed Successfully".
Pending vs Settled amount

Pending amount is the part of an approved claim not yet paid (claimed minus what has been settled). Settled amount is the total already paid via Cash, Bank and Cheque. The dashboard tracks both across companies, locations, grades, departments and sections.
Finance Dashboard

A read-only analytics tab: claimed/settled/pending bars, a Cash/Bank/Cheque distribution, and per-group summary cards (chosen via Show Group) so Finance can see where money is committed and outstanding.

concepts: Ticket lifecycle

A ticket starts Open when raised, becomes In Progress once an authority replies, and is Closed when resolved. A closed ticket can be Re-Opened if the issue recurs, which puts it back into the active queue.
TAT / SLA

TAT (Turn-Around Time) is the target time to resolve a ticket. When a ticket is closed the system flags whether TAT was Achieved (Yes/No); the card colour turns green if met and red if missed, so SLA health is visible at a glance.
Reply vs Reply & Close

Reply posts a message and keeps the ticket open for further conversation. Reply & Close posts your message and closes the ticket in one step. Both add your message (and any attachments) to the ticket timeline.
Forward

Forwarding hands a ticket to another employee (the eligible forward list is loaded per ticket). Use it when the query should be handled by someone else; the ticket stays open and the new assignee can respond.
Watcher
A watcher is someone added to follow a ticket without being its owner. Watchers can see updates on the ticket; the Watchers tab lists who is currently watching.
Ticket Dashboard

A permission-gated analytics tab showing ticket summaries and performance trend charts for the current and last month (e.g. hours taken / volume), so managers can monitor help-desk load and responsiveness.
rules: Raising a ticket requires Category, Sub Category, Priority, Subject and a description; the Submit stays blocked until all are filled.
Sub Category only loads after a Category is chosen — selecting it first shows "Please Select Category".
Reply and Reply & Close both require message text, otherwise you get "Please Enter Reply Text"; forwarding requires text too ("Please Enter Forward Text").
Closing a ticket from the action bar needs a remark, otherwise "Please Give the Message" is shown.
A ticket moves through Open → In Progress → Closed, and a closed ticket can come back as Re-Opened.
On close, TAT Achieved is recorded as Yes/No and the card border/colour reflects it (green = TAT met, red = missed).
Managers/HR land on the assigned-tickets / dashboard view; regular employees see their own ticket list.

concepts: Time sheet / log time
A record of how many hours you worked on a given day, broken down by project and task. Each entry is one block of work; the calendar and KPI strip add them up per day, per week and per month.
Client vs Project vs Task

A Client is the customer the work is for, a Project is a piece of work delivered for that client, and a Task is a specific activity inside the project. When clients are enabled you choose Client -> Project -> Task in that order; otherwise you go straight to Project -> Task.
Time Spent (duration) vs Start / End time

Companies log time one of two ways. In duration mode you type the total Time Spent directly as HH:MM. In hourly mode you enter a Start Time and End Time and the system calculates Time Spent for you (and blocks an end time earlier than the start).
Status: Pending / Approved / Rejected

When timesheet workflow is enabled, a new entry starts as Pending and is sent for approval. A manager can Approve or Reject it. Only Pending entries can still be edited; once Approved or Rejected the entry is locked for viewing only.
History Log

A reporting tab (separate from the live calendar) where you select one or more employees, a From / To date range and a status, then click Generate to pull a grid of past timesheet records you can review and export.
Masters: Client / Project / Manpower

Setup screens for project managers / HR. Client Master adds clients (with their contacts and assigned resources), Project Master adds projects (with estimates and task lists), and Manpower Master maps which employees (resources) are available to be logged against projects.
rules: Every time log requires Date, Project, Task, Time Spent and Description; Start Time and End Time are also required when the company logs time by start/end (hourly) rather than as a typed duration
When the company is configured to enter Start / End time, Time Spent is calculated automatically and must be a valid HH:MM (00:00-23:59); End Time cannot be before Start Time

If a past-days limit is set, you can only log or edit entries within the allowed number of past days (otherwise only today)
Logging on a weekly off, holiday or approved-leave day is blocked unless the company allows it for that day type
When timesheet workflow is on, only Pending entries can be edited; Approved and Rejected entries are read-only
Old multi-day entries cannot be edited

next: Open the Employee Assets tab and select an employee to review their assigned assets, or use the master tabs to set up groups, types, stores and stock first.

concepts: Asset Group vs Asset Type vs Asset Store

An Asset Group is the broad category (e.g. IT Equipment). An Asset Type is a specific kind within a group (e.g. Laptop) carrying rules like consumable, max quantity, return period and serial-number requirement. An Asset Store is a physical/logical stock location, owned by a Super User, from which stock is issued.
Consumable vs Non-Consumable

Consumable assets (e.g. stationery) are not expected back, so they have no return period. Non-Consumable assets (e.g. laptops) are tracked for return; they carry a Return Period and unit, and the return/recall flow applies to them.
Serial number requirement

An asset type can require a unique serial number per item. When required, each stock item is tracked individually by its serial/service tag, which is what links a specific physical unit to the employee it is assigned to.
Return Period
The time within which a non-consumable asset is expected to be returned. It is set on the asset type (a positive number plus a unit) and drives return tracking once the asset is assigned.
Stock vs assigned asset

Stock is an item held in a store and not yet given out. Assigning it to an employee turns it into an assigned asset that appears on that employee's Employee Assets tab. Recall pulls it back into stock; Return is the employee-initiated handover back.
Assign / Recall / Return / Receive lifecycle

Assign issues a stock item to an employee. Return is raised against an assigned asset (with a comment) and marks it Pending Return. Recall lets the authority pull an asset back. The receiving authority then confirms receipt to close the loop and return the item to stock.
Store Super User & Participants

A store has a Super User (the owner/manager responsible for its stock) and Participants (others who can operate it). Being a store manager also unlocks the Add Stocks tab even without the general 25.1 permission.
rules: Which tabs you see depends on permissions: Employee Assets needs 25.0; Asset Group / Types / Store need 25.1; Add Stocks needs stock permission (25.1 or being a store manager) and is hidden on mobile.

Asset Store: Store Name, Super User and Participants are all required.

A return requires a return comment before it can be submitted.

concepts: Category vs Sub Category

Category is fixed to Company Policy here. The Sub Category (e.g. Leave Policy, Travel Policy, Data Security Policy, Employee Hand Book) is what you choose to file or find a document under, so policies stay organised by topic.
Targeting audience (Company / Location / Grade / Employment Type)

When HR uploads a policy they scope it to specific companies, locations, grades and employment types. Employees only see the policies whose audience matches them; selecting all options for a field means it applies to everyone.
Digital Acceptance

A setting per policy controlling whether employees must digitally acknowledge it: Not Required, Menu Disable, or Menu Enable. The Edit (Digital Acceptance) dialog lets HR change this so a policy can be made acknowledgement-mandatory after upload.
Table view vs Card view

Two ways to browse the same policy documents: a dense grid (Table) for scanning many rows, or visual cards (Card) showing the file type, target audience and quick Preview/Download/Edit/Delete actions.
Preview vs Download

Preview opens the document in the in-app viewer (only for PDFs and images). Download saves the original file to your device with a timestamped name, and is available whenever the policy is marked downloadable.

concepts: Profile tabs

The profile is split into tabs: Basic Info (skills, hobbies, manager, holidays, payslip, swipes), Employment (designation, grade, department, reporting, shift, attendance & weekly off), Payment (statutory applicability, bank details, salary structure), Personal (personal details, contact, emergency contact, dependents, qualifications, experience, visa / passport), Custom (company-defined custom fields), Documents, Salary (structure, revision history) and History.
Edit Profile (name & About)

The pencil next to your name opens the Edit Profile dialog: First Name (required), Middle Name, Last Name and an About / summary (AI-assisted, up to 1000 characters). It saves directly; if nothing changed it reports "No changes found".
Skills & Hobbies

On Basic Info you maintain Skills and Hobbies as chips - add, click a chip to edit it, remove with the x, or drag to reorder. Each is stored as a comma-separated list. You must enter a value before Add is enabled.
Profile photo vs cover photo

The avatar edit icon changes your profile picture; the cover edit icon changes the banner. Both open the same uploader which lets you crop the image (and, where facial attendance is enabled, capture from the camera). JPEG/PNG only, under 2 MB.
Statutory applicability (PF / UAN / ESI / PAN)

The Statutory Applicability card holds your statutory identifiers - PF number, UAN (Universal Account Number for provident fund), ESI number, PAN, NPS percentage and EPS flag - and is where PAN / Aadhaar documents are attached. Custom PF and Voluntary PF (VPF) sub-screens exist for extra contribution rules.
Salary structure & CTC

The Salary tab shows your salary structure - the breakup of allowances into monthly and yearly amounts - plus revision history comparing previous and revised monthly CTC (cost to company) and the percentage change between revisions.
Cost centre weightage
Cost centre allocation splits your salary cost across one or more cost centres by a weightage (percentage) so payroll can apportion the expense; the weightages are expected to total 100%.
Dependents vs medical dependents

Dependents (Personal tab) are family members recorded for PF / ESI / gratuity / insurance eligibility with name, relationship, date of birth, education and address. Medical dependents are the subset added specifically against a medical / insurance claim (name and relation).
Swipe card
A swipe / access card record holds the card ID, issue date and valid-from / valid-to dates used for attendance and door access. This card dialog is a preview layout in this build.
Attendance & weekly off
The Attendance link opens your attendance dashboard. Weekly off (shown as "Rest Day" or "Second Weekly Off" depending on the company setting) is part of the employment / attendance configuration.

A punch can be recorded via Web Login (the employee checks in from the web/app, capturing a selfie and GPS location) or via a Bio Metric/Swipe device. The filter lets you view either source; web punches carry the selfie + map location.

Productive vs Non-Productive hours

The calendar shows each day as a coloured event (leave, holiday, weekly-off, attendance). Switching to List view shows the same pay period as an attendance grid where each row has a View Punches action to inspect that day's swipes.
Event colours / legend

Every event type returned for the period becomes a coloured legend chip (its colour comes from the server) plus an All chip. Ticking a chip filters the calendar to that event type; All shows everything. Pending applications and approved leaves are distinct event types and so get their own colours.
Applying for leave

Approval routing

concepts: Compensatory Off (C-Off)
A day of paid time off you earn by working on a holiday or your scheduled week-off. You raise this request to claim that earned day back later.
Work Date vs Compensatory Date

Work Date is the holiday or week-off you actually worked. Compensatory Date is the day you want to take off in return. The Compensatory Date only appears (and is required) when your company links the leave and C-Off workflows.
Full Day / Half Day work
Indicates how much extra work you did on the Work Date. Half Day counts as 0.5 of a comp-off; Full Day counts as 1.
First Half / Second Half

Approval flow & status

concepts: Old vs New tax regime

Two ways your tax is computed. The Old regime lets you claim most exemptions and Chapter VI-A deductions (80C, 80D, HRA, etc.); the New regime has lower slab rates but allows very few deductions. The Old / New toggle re-calculates the figures, and the Detail card shows both side by side so you can compare before submitting.
Section 80C

The most common deduction bucket (life insurance, PPF/EPF, ELSS, children's tuition fees, principal repayment of a home loan, NSC, etc.), capped at the limit shown on the card. Declare each investment's amount in its pending field and upload the proof inside the 80C dialog.
Section 80D / 80DD / 80U / 80DDB

Health and disability-related deductions: 80D for medical insurance premium, 80DD for treatment of a handicapped dependent, 80U for the employee's own permanent physical disability, and 80DDB for medical treatment of a senior citizen. Each is declared in its own dialog with its own limit.
Section 80CCD / 80CCD(2)

80CCD covers contributions to the National Pension Scheme (NPS); 80CCD(2) is the employer NPS contribution that is also allowed under the New regime. These appear as separate cards with their own limits.
HRA exemption

House Rent Allowance exemption from the HRA dialog. It is computed from HRA received from payroll, rent paid minus 10% of basic salary, and 50% (metro) or 40% (non-metro) of basic salary — the lowest of these is the Final Exemption Amount. You can declare rent monthly or annually and attach rent receipts / landlord PAN where required.
House Property

Income or loss from a let-out or self-occupied house — rental income, home-loan interest, municipal tax and standard deduction — declared in the same dialog as HRA. A self-occupied property loss reduces your taxable income up to the limit shown.
Chapter VI-A deductions

The income-tax sections (80C, 80CCD, 80D, 80E, 80G, 80TTA, 80U, etc.) that let you reduce taxable income under the Old regime. Each card on this screen maps to one such section with its own maximum limit.
Other Exemptions

Salary-component exemptions handled in the Others dialog — conveyance, medical reimbursement, children's education, LTA, fuel allowance, mobile reimbursement, food coupons and other exemptions — each with its own proof upload.
Income From Other Sources
Income outside salary that is still taxable — for example bonus, ex-gratia, gratuity and interest income — declared in the Others dialog so it is included in your total taxable income.
Perks (perquisites)
Taxable benefits your employer provides on top of salary (the "Perks" card). Their taxable value is added to your income; declare the relevant amounts and proofs in the Perks dialog.
Previous Employer Tax
If you joined mid-year, the taxable income and TDS already deducted by your previous employer (with company name, TAN, PAN proofs) so this employer can compute tax correctly for the full year.
Declared vs approved (proof submitted)

What you enter is "pending/declared" and shown in the Saved / Pending Approve columns; once the IT team verifies the uploaded proof it becomes "approved" and read-only. The Detail card compares Saved, Pending Approve and Approved values.
Projection vs Actual

Early in the year your declaration is a projection (estimate) of what you will invest; later it becomes actual once proofs are submitted. The "View Projection" button shows the previous projected declaration when the year is in projection mode.
ClearTax / Form 16 / Form 12B

ClearTax is an integration to file your return online using your generated Form 16. Form 16 (Part A & B) is the TDS certificate you can download for a financial year; Form 12B captures income from a previous employer for mid-year joiners and is available to managers and resigned employees.

Amounts subtracted from your gross pay — such as provident fund, professional tax, income tax (TDS) or other recoveries. The Total row sums them.
Net Pay
The take-home amount credited to your bank account: total earnings minus total deductions for the month.

concepts: Salary advance

An advance is money paid to you upfront and then recovered from your future salary in instalments. Unlike a loan it is typically interest-free — you repay only the principal, split evenly across the chosen number of months.
EMI (instalment)

The fixed amount deducted from your salary each month until the advance is fully repaid. Here it is simply the advance amount divided by the number of installments (rounded up), so a higher number of installments means a smaller monthly deduction.
Recovery / repayment from salary

Once an advance is approved and disbursed, each month’s EMI is automatically deducted (recovered) from your pay. The Outstanding Balance and EMIs-Paid figures track how much is left and how many instalments have already been recovered.
Advance status lifecycle

An advance moves from Apply (you submit the application) to Approval (Pending until an approver acts, then Approved) to Recovery (instalments deducted each month) and finally Closed once the full amount is repaid. The status chip on each card and the Active vs Closed counts in the summary reflect this lifecycle.
Calculate EMI vs Apply

Calculate EMI validates your request on the server and previews the monthly instalment. Only after a successful calculation does the Apply button appear, letting you submit the application for approval.
Repayment schedule & chart
Opening an advance shows the Installments grid (each due month, amount and status) alongside a cumulative-repayment column chart, so you can see exactly how the advance is being paid down over time.

The End Month is auto-calculated from the Start Month plus the number of installments (it cannot be edited)
The Start Month is snapped to the 1st of the month and cannot be earlier than the first day of the current month
The Application Date is fixed to today and is sent with the request
You must Calculate EMI first — the Apply button only appears after the EMI is calculated, and is disabled while the form is invalid
EMI = the advance amount divided evenly across the number of installments (principal repayment, rounded up); a salary advance carries no separate interest unless your setup applies one
Calculate EMI runs an eligibility check on the server; if it fails, the validation message is shown and the EMI is not calculated
A new advance only shows on this screen once it is approved — the Apply button raises a request, it does not disburse money
The repayment progress bar and gauge reflect EMIs paid out of the total instalments
tips: Adjusting the Amount, Start Month, or No. of Installments resets a previously calculated EMI — click Calculate EMI again before applying
Use the Purpose field to clearly state why you need the advance; it helps the approver decide
Open an advance card to track exactly which months have been recovered from your salary

concepts: EMI (Equated Monthly Instalment)

The fixed amount you repay each month. The screen computes it from the loan amount, annual interest rate and number of instalments using the standard reducing-balance formula; for a 0% interest loan it is simply the amount divided by the number of instalments.
Tenure / No. of Instalments
How many monthly instalments the loan runs for (1 to 500). It sets the loan duration in months and, together with the start month, determines the end month automatically.
Interest Amount
The total interest you pay over the life of the loan: (EMI x number of instalments) minus the loan amount. It is shown alongside the EMI after you calculate, and is zero for a 0% loan.
Guarantor

A colleague who backs your loan. It is only required for loan types configured as guarantor-required. While the loan is still in the guarantor stage you can swap the guarantor for a different eligible employee from the loan-details view.
Loan status lifecycle

Outstanding Balance vs Disbursed

concepts: Leave encashment
Converting unused, accrued leave days into cash instead of taking them as time off. You request a number of days against a leave type and, once approved, they are paid out.
Available balance
The leave days you currently have accrued for a given leave type in the selected year. It is shown per row in the Encashment Balances grid.
Encashable days
The maximum number of days that may be encashed for that leave type (it can be lower than your available balance). The add dialog pre-fills this as the default Days to Encash, which you can reduce.
Request to approval flow
Saving the dialog creates a Pending request. An approver then Approves or Rejects it; the outcome appears in the Encashment Status grid. Only approved requests lead to a payout.

concepts: Local Claim (reimbursement)

A request to be paid back for a local business expense such as travel, food or other costs. You record the reason, mode, travel date, route/distance and amount; once approved and paid by HR it is "settled".
Claim status lifecycle

Waiting for Submission (a draft you have saved but not sent) -> Pending (sent and awaiting approval) -> Approved (cleared by approvers, not yet paid) or Rejected (sent back - you can edit and resend). After approval HR settles it, moving it to Paid in Cash, Paid via Bank or Cheque Paid.
Send For Approval

Mode

Settled (Cash / Bank / Cheque)

concepts: Headcount
The total number of active employees in the selected month for your filtered population, shown with a male/female breakdown and each gender's share as a percentage of the total (the diversity ratio).
Diversity ratio (Male / Female %)
The proportion of the headcount that is male versus female, displayed beside the raw male and female counts so you can gauge gender balance for the selected group and period.
Gross / Compensation

Total gross pay for the population, with its period-over-period change as a percentage and a Gain/Loss trend flag. The Gross chart plots Actual vs Earned gross month by month so you can see cost-to-company movement over the selected window.
Salary Changes vs Loss of Pay

Salary Changes summarises the salary amount, its percentage change, a trend flag and the count of affected employees. Loss of Pay (LOP) is the deduction value for unpaid absence, with its own amount, percentage, trend and employee count.
Attrition Rate
How many people left relative to the workforce in the period, shown as a count plus a percentage and a Gain/Loss trend versus the prior period. A rising attrition rate signals retention risk.
Joinees vs Resignees
Joinees are employees who started and Resignees are those who left in the period. The trend chart overlays both as splines so you can see whether hiring is keeping pace with exits.
Attrition Reason

A breakdown of resignations by stated reason (e.g. career change, relocation), each shown with a resignation count and its percentage share of total exits, to highlight the biggest drivers of attrition.
Attendance gauges
Four circular gauges showing the Present, Absent, Leaves and Comp-Off shares of the workforce as percentages for the period, giving a quick read on attendance health.
Overtime Hours vs Overtime Compensation
Two charts: overtime hours worked per month and the monetary overtime amount per month. They are separately permissioned (17.0.6.6 and 17.0.6.5) and laid out side by side only when you can see both.
Period tabs (Month / Quarter / Half Year / Year)

Controls the analysis window. Month uses the picked month; Last 3 Months looks back 2 months, Last 6 Months looks back 5, and Last 1 Year looks back 11, all ending at the picked month. The 'Selected Period' line confirms the exact from/to dates in use.

concepts: Attended (Present) vs Absent

Attended counts the days you were physically present (and in the details dialog, Physical Present). Absents counts working days with no presence recorded. Both are categories in the donut and rows in the Quick Summary.
On Leave (Leaves)
Days covered by an approved leave for the period, shown as the Leaves slice/row. These are distinct from Weekly Offs and Holidays, which are non-working days rather than consumed leave.
Late Entries / Late Hours / Late Deductions

Late Entries (lateInDays) is the count of days you clocked in after your shift start. Late Hours is the total late duration, and Late Deductions is the leave deducted as a penalty for repeated lateness. These appear in the View Attendance details dialog.
Attendance percentage

Each metric's percentage is its value divided by Total Days for the period (e.g. Paid Days / Total Days). It is what colours the accent bar in the Quick Summary and sizes each donut slice. Hour-based metrics show no percentage.
Paid Days
The number of days you are paid for in the period - typically present days plus paid leaves, weekly offs and holidays. It is the primary metric the summary progress indicator tracks.
Weekly Offs vs Rest Days

Weekly Offs are your scheduled non-working days. Rest Days is the same idea shown under a different label and only appears (in the details dialog) when your global setting WeeklyOffShowAsRestday is enabled.
C-off / Comp Off
Compensatory off - leave earned for working on an off day or holiday. It shows as the C-off slice in the donut and as Comp Off in the View Attendance details.

Generate the statutory compliance outputs for a selected month — the PF ECR text file, the ESI monthly upload file and the state-wise Professional Tax (PT) challan. You can: Pick employees with the multi-select (use the filter button to refine by company, location, department, designation or section); Choose the return month with the Choose Month picker; PF ECR: select employees and month, then Get ECR Details to download the PF ECR file; ESI Monthly Upload: Generate to preview the ESI data in the grid, then Generate ESI Upload to download the upload file.

Select employees and a date or month range, choose the columns and options for the report variant, then preview the data on screen or download it as an Excel file. You can: Pick employees with the Employees dropdown, or open the Filter sidebar to narrow by department, location and other criteria; Choose a date range (Swipe / Enhanced Monthly) or a month range (Leaves Summary / Increment) for the report; For the Swipe Report, tick the columns to include (Shift, Status, InTime, OutTime, Time Spent, Late Minutes, Late Penality, Early Minutes, Early Penality, HalfDays, Penality Status, Attendance, Attendance Type) using Select All or the individual checkboxes; Toggle Show Incident Info and Vertical Report on the Swipe Report.

Generate and download payroll outputs for a selected month — the bank salary-disbursement file, the PayRegister (filtered or pivot), Accounting JV, Variance and Asset summaries. You can: Pick employees with the multi-select (use the filter button to refine by company, location, department, designation or section); Choose the salary month (or a From/To month range using the Period checkbox where available); Bank Transfer: choose the template (Salary / Loan / Advance), the Bank Name(s) and a Bank Template, then Download the bank file; PayRegister With Filters: add Allowances, Deductions, Custom Fields, Listing Fields, Other Wages and Attendance / Loans-Advances breakups, then View or export to Excel.

Build and run a management-information (MIS) report for the selected employees — the exact report shown depends on which report you opened (Employee Master, Employee Listing, Attrition or Web Login). You can: Pick the employees with the Filter (funnel) button; the count next to it shows how many are selected; Choose the month (or From / To dates) the report should cover; For Employee Listing: select a saved Form Name, then choose the Sequence Report Fields and Personal Fields to show as columns; Create or edit a reusable column layout with the "Create Sequence Fields Form" button.
